claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories with one package per repository, as its recommended strategy for publishing packages.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository, and its version is the Git tag on that repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.

Semver-tagged releases are required only for publishing to the Private Registry; source-based packages referenced directly from a Pulumi.yaml file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit) regardless of semver validity.
An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically with per-language SDKs published to feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
An executable-based package's version is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights how Pulumi consumes packages.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components to secure and operate it.
One PulumiPlugin.yaml at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
Using a single monorepo with one giant package for all components forfeits meaningful semantic versioning, and Pulumi does not recommend it.
When unrelated components share a package, every package release versions every component the same way, which violates semver.
A cross-reference exists to the Publishing packages guide at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/packages/publishing-packages/.
